theme: योग का अर्थ है संकल्प का त्याग; मन को साधना आवश्यक है। / Yoga means relinquishing selfish resolve; the mind must be trained, not merely stirred.
context: Krishna deepens the meaning of yoga by clarifying the inner quality required for it. He says that the renunciation meant here is not only external withdrawal from work, but surrender of saṅkalpa, the mental intention shaped by self-interest. Without this inner letting-go, no one becomes a true yogi.
contextHindi: श्रीकृष्ण योग के अर्थ को और गहराई से समझा रहे हैं। यहाँ ‘संन्यास’ का मतलब केवल बाहरी कर्मों का छोड़ना नहीं है, बल्कि ‘सङ्कल्प’ का त्याग है—वह मानसिक निश्चय जो स्वार्थ, लोभ और अपने लाभ के लिए बनता है। बिना इस आंतरिक छोड़ने के कोई व्यक्ति सच्चा योगी नहीं बनता।
sanskritDevanagari:
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुर्योगं तं विद्धि पाण्डव |
न ह्यसंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पो योगी भवति कश्चन ||६-२||
transliteration:
yaṃ saṃnyāsamiti prāhuryogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava .
na hyasaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||6-2||

wordByWord.meaning: Renunciation; the letting-go of attachment, possessiveness, and self-centered motive.
Yoga, union, steadiness, and disciplined inner harmony.
Volition, resolve, or mental intention, especially when shaped by desire and ego.
One whose mind no longer runs by selfish plotting and craving.

spokenHindi: यह श्लोक बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि श्रीकृष्ण यहाँ योग को ‘संन्यास’ से जोड़ते हैं, लेकिन केवल बाहरी संन्यास नहीं, आंतरिक संन्यास। ‘सङ्कल्प’ शब्द का अर्थ है मन का वह प्रयोजन जो हम अपने लिए बनाते हैं—‘मैं चाहूँगा, मैं पाऊँगा, मैं इस तरह करूँगा’ जैसी मानसिक योजना। अगर यह संकल्प अभी भी बना है, तब तक मन की दिशा आत्म-केन्द्रित रहती है। योग की शुरुआत तब होती है जब मन अपने स्वार्थी उद्देश्य को थोड़ा-थोड़ा छोड़ता है। इसलिए कृष्ण कहते हैं, ‘असंन्यस्तसङ्कल्पः’—जो अपने संकल्प को नहीं छोड़ा, वह योगी नहीं बन सकता। यह श्लोक ध्यान के लिए बहुत सीधा और कठोर सत्य देता है: मन को अंदर से शुद्ध करना पड़ता है।
clearEnglish: This verse states that the yoga Krishna means here is not merely an external lifestyle label. It is a change in the inner will. The word saṅkalpa points to the mental decision-making that is often shaped by craving, ego, and expectation. Krishna says that one who has not renounced such inward plotting does not become a yogi. This does not mean the mind becomes empty or lifeless; it means the will becomes less selfish and more aligned with truth, duty, and clarity. The practical challenge is not only what we do, but what we secretly decide in the mind. A person can outwardly appear disciplined while still operating from personal ambition. Yoga asks for a deeper integrity: to loosen the grip of self-centered intention, and let attention rest in what is steady and true.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The direct teaching is that yoga is the renunciation of saṅkalpa, not merely the renunciation of external work. A yogi is not someone who has merely left an activity; he is someone whose inner intention is no longer driven by desire-based plotting.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A reasonable conclusion is that spiritual progress depends on reducing self-constructed motives. When the mind is less driven by personal gain, it becomes more available for meditation and discernment.

interpretationPerspectives.label: COMMENTARY
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The Divine Life Society note emphasizes that the inner mind often hides desires even when outward conduct seems disciplined. That is precisely why Krishna here focuses on saṅkalpa as the target of renunciation.

practicalApplication.label: Watch the inner script
practicalApplication.text: Notice the hidden planning in your mind: 'I need this, I must get that, I deserve this.' Before acting, gently ask whether the intention is rooted in duty or in wanting to win.

practicalApplication.label: Short detachment practice
practicalApplication.text: For five minutes, choose one small action and do it with minimal planning for personal gain. Then notice how the mind settles.

reflectionQuestion: Which of my inner intentions are still framed by desire, and which are shaped by clarity and responsibility?
reflectionQuestionHindi: मेरे अंदर से कौन-से निश्चय अभी भी इच्छा के आधार पर हैं, और कौन से विवेक और कर्तव्य के आधार पर हैं?
